You leave the unanswered offer where it is and finish the last of the tart while the dining hall empties around you.

The garden door shuts behind Ashara and Rashid. From the common room, cards crack against the table near the fire; someone gives a brief, dissatisfied groan at a hand gone wrong. A server collects your plate and replaces it with nothing.

Soon the long table is mostly candlelight, cleared silver, and the fading warmth of dinner.
